summary:
FireScope – Global Fire Intelligence is a web-based prototype developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing the challenge “Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots.”

The platform brings together active-fire hotspot observations from NASA FIRMS, including MODIS and VIIRS satellite data, to help users explore fire activity through a unified interface.

FireScope provides an interactive global fire map, hotspot visualization, historical exploration, and a Dark Canvas experience to make satellite observations easier to understand.

By presenting observations from two satellite systems together, FireScope aims to make fire-related data more accessible and support awareness and exploration of global fire activity.

Important: Satellite hotspots represent thermal anomalies and are not necessarily confirmed wildfires. The prototype's matching and harmonization approach requires further scientific validation before operational use.
details:
Data sources:

  • NASA FIRMS (Fire Information for Resource Management System)
  • MODIS active-fire observations
  • VIIRS active-fire observations

Development tools:

  • Visual Studio Code
  • Git and GitHub
  • Render (application hosting)
  • Antigravity (AI-assisted development)
  • ChatGPT (AI-assisted planning, explanations and documentation)

Additional software libraries, map resources, imagery, icons and fonts used in the application should also be listed with their applicable sources and licences.
